column1: # The level 2 swipe corpus (bead tla-7xql.5, epic tla-7xql).
# 48 items in one template, the pilot described in swipe/level2/TEMPLATES.tsv.
# Every item pins a STEP and asks whether a step formula holds across it, so
# the model screen carries two states rather than one.
# swipe/level2/render.sh builds that screen and swipe/level2/bake.sh measures
# the verdict.
# Rows are tab-delimited and carry the literal marker ITEM in field 1, so
# prose in this file can never be read as data. Read rows with awk -F'\t' or
# cut, never with IFS=$'\t' read: tab is IFS whitespace, so a run of tabs
# collapses and an empty field vanishes.
# AN ITEM ROW. Fifteen fields, in order. Fields 1 to 11 keep their level 0 and
# level 1 meanings so harness/swipe/stemblind.sh reads this table with --items
# and no code change, 12 and 13 keep level 1's, and 14 and 15 are what a
# pinned STEP adds:
#    1  marker      the literal ITEM
#    2  id          L2-<template>-<nn>, stable, never renumbered
#    3  template    S1, resolving to a TEMPLATES.tsv row
#    4  ask         the tag shown WITH the question: step or always. It names
#                   which of the epic's question kinds the line is and it does
#                   NOT determine the answer
#    5  kind        the item's own kind: true, false, vacuous, illformed,
#                   wronglevel or unparsed. The reader never sees it
#    6  swipe       right, left or down. Derived from field 5 by the bake
#    7  rc          the exit code of the PROPERTY run. Written by the bake
#    8  pin_states  how many distinct states the pin admits. Always 2 at this
#                   rung, and the bake's postcondition is what says so
#    9  claim       the single line the reader answers
#   10  vacuity     a witness that the claim is vacuous, or -
#   11  flash       the one line shown after the swipe, always present. On a
#                   false, vacuous, illformed, wronglevel or unparsed item it
#                   is the correction. On a true item it is the reason the
#                   claim holds, because there is nothing to correct about a
#                   true statement. Frank ruled on 2026-10-18
#   12  model       the reading/ module the item is about
#   13  pre         the pinned state the step starts from, a TLA+ conjunction
#   14  post        the step's own formula, a TLA+ conjunction over primes
#   15  binds       the pin's own constants, as assignments, or -
#   awk -F'\t' '$1 == "ITEM" && $12 == "Tickets"' swipe/level2/ITEMS.tsv
#   grep '^ITEM' swipe/level2/ITEMS.tsv | cut -f5,12 | sort | uniq -c
# FIELDS 6, 7 AND 8 ARE OWNED BY swipe/level2/bake.sh. Do not hand-edit them.
# Field 5 is the author's PREDICTION and the bake is there to contradict it.
# THE REFUTED KIND MAPS TO TWO EXIT CODES AND FIELD 7 HOLDS THE MEASURED ONE.
# Hazard H1 on the epic says to read {12, 13} as one answer and never to
# predict which, so the bake checks membership in a set rather than equality
# against a number. Every refutation at this rung measured 13, because a step
# formula is checked in the temporal pass rather than lifted to an invariant,
# and the channel still accepts 12 because H1 is about what a generator may
# assume rather than about what one build printed.
# FIELD 8 IS A CONSTANT HERE AND IT WAS A VARIABLE AT LEVEL 1. A pinned step
# is one initial state and one successor, so TLCGet("distinct") is 2, and
# hazard H3 on the epic is exactly the statement that it had better be. One
# number catches a Pre that admits two states and a Post that admits a branch,
# both of which mean a SET of behaviors was pinned. Measured: a Post of
# next' \in {1, 2} reads 10 against 2 and 0 against 3.
# A PIN CONSTANT IS HOW A MODEL VALUE GETS NAMED, and field 15 carries it.
# Ini == holder = s1 fails at rc 150 with a semantic error, because s1 is a
# .cfg model value and not an identifier the module can name. The pin module
# declares CONSTANT H1 and the .cfg assigns H1 = s1. Four of the seven models
# here carry model values, so this is the common case rather than the corner.
# A CLAIM MAY ONLY NAME A DEFINITION THE SCREEN SHOWS, plus vars and the pin
# constants. Decision D7 withholds Init, Next and Spec, so no claim names one.
# vars is the exception this rung adds: it is the subscript 77 percent of the
# published corpus writes, the level 1 strip removes it because no action
# reaches it, and swipe/level2/render.sh puts it back for exactly that reason.
# NO CLAIM USES <>, WF_ OR SF_, AND THAT IS A CORRECTNESS RULE. A pinned
# behavior carries no fairness, so the behavior that stutters at the pre-state
# forever is admitted and every liveness claim is refuted whatever it says.
# Measured: []<>(next = 1) reads 13 on a step that does set next to 1. An item
# built on one of those is false for a reason the pin never had an opinion
# about. The gate bans the three operators outright.
# ITEMS ARE AUTHORED IN MATCHED GROUPS, which is what keeps the stem-blind
# gate green. The unit is either a four, one item of each of four kinds built
# from one pinned step, or a pair, a true and a false built from one pinned
# step. Six fours and twelve pairs is 48, and it lands the mix at 18 true, 18
# false and 12 down without anybody counting. That arithmetic is level 1's.
# THE SWIPE MIX IS LEVEL 0'S AND SO IS THE KIND MIX UNDER down. Right is 18 of
# 48, so the base rate is 0.3750 and the power table in swipe/README.md
# transfers unchanged. Under down this rung splits 12 the same way level 1
# does, 4 vacuous, 3 illformed, 3 wronglevel and 2 unparsed, because the
# channel has the same six kinds even though two of them read different exit
# codes here.
# THE SUBSCRIPT IS BALANCED ACROSS THE LABELS ON PURPOSE. Four items share one
# pinned step and differ only in the subscript, so if the subscript alone
# predicted the label the corpus would measure nothing. Every variable that
# stutters in a vacuous item also carries a true item and a false item on
# another step, and the two Nim units ship the SAME claim text over two pins
# with opposite labels. harness/test-swipe-subscript.sh runs the stem-blind
# probe at the full surface and again over the subscript alone.
# NO ITEM DEPENDS ON \div. TLC 2026.07.31.184830 breaks the contract its own
# Naturals.tla states for a negative dividend, bead tla-7n7e is open on it,
# and \div 0 inside a step formula reads rc 255 rather than the 75 every other
# evaluation failure here reads. No claim or pin uses \div at all.
# FIELD 11 IS NOT OPTIONAL. L2 on the epic: a falsehood is reproduced later at
# .19 with no feedback, .15 with a bare verdict and .04 with the verdict plus
# the correction. The gate rejects a blank one and a stub.
